name: Internazionale 2009/10 (Mourinho)
scopeNote: Inter of the treble season under Mourinho, 2009-08-08 (Supercoppa, period fixed by the user; the Supercoppa date and result were not re-verified in a mined page, only that the Super Cup was lost to Lazio) to 2010-05-22 (Champions League final v Bayern). Style: a compact mid/low block with fast counters (Wilson: 'we managed to play and win with counters'), not a pressing or possession side; 'catenaccio'/'parking the bus' is the press label, while sources describe mid-block 4-4-2 / 4-5-1 and 4-2-3-1 variants. 4-3-1-2 start with Sneijder as trequartista and the 4-2-3-1 from the Chelsea tie are reported by search summaries and the Blitz projection but only the Stamford Bridge 4-2-3-1 is verified in a mined page. Wilson uses a 4-3-3 as Mourinho's basic model (Chelsea and Inter), conflicting with 4-2-3-1 labels. 2008/09 (Mancini) and 2010/11 (Benitez) excluded; the FourFourTwo Nov 2010 zonal quote is Real Madrid era and kept unverified. Coaches' Voice masterclass is paywalled, so its content is taken from a Goal.com report of the same video.
openQuestions: Messi marking at Camp Nou/San Siro: Mourinho (Coaches' Voice via Goal.com) says 'we didn't play man-to-man' and describes zonal handover with Zanetti, Motta, Cambiasso; a Substack (Maldonado, 2025, first leg) says Messi was 'man-marked everywhere he went' and that Pandev tucked in to man-mark. Likely loose wording for tight, zone-based close marking; Mourinho's primary account preferred.

Date and exact shift from 4-3-1-2 to 4-2-3-1: the Guardian piece (pressreader, unreadable) reportedly says mid-season with Eto'o on the left; inter.it states a 4-2-3-1 at Chelsea on 2010-03-16 and its lineup shows Sneijder behind Pandev, Milito, Eto'o. Wilson says Mourinho's basic model is 4-3-3.
Final shape vs Bayern: some sources say 4-2-3-1, one summary says 4-4-2 diamond; no mined tier A-B page states it explicitly.
Tier A coverage is thin: Coaches' Voice is paywalled; no Spielverlagerung/StatsBomb/Tifo page for this season was found.
Possession figures differ: Wilson says 16% at Camp Nou in one article (preview) and 'more than twice' of 33% in the other; FourFourTwo says 24%.

statedView.quote: We didn't play man-to-man but Zanetti, Motta, Cambiasso, everybody was responsible for any position that Messi could go.
We are a very compact team; we have little distance between the players, and we managed to play and win with counters, and this is typical for our team.
It was a provocation in a football sense when before the match [Van Gaal] said Inter is a defensive team, not playing with the same attacking spirit, and I wanted to play with counters.

They are going to have the ball more than us, much more than us obviously, because many many times they were moving the ball without hurting [us] and we must be mentally strong to cope with that. Let them have the ball but not create many chances.

I told him that if he wins the Champions League with Barcelona, he won't be doing anything extraordinary, seeing as the Catalans have won it twice in three years. I like doing something extraordinary, not what's normal.
